key_insight: Ligand-engineered AgBiS2 nanocrystal films enable thicker near-infrared absorbers and 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with perovskite sub-cells.
engineering_relevance: Solution-phase processing offers a route to scalable tandem photovoltaics with improved near-infrared harvesting and promising storage stability.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated, thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-light-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
